title: NTSB safety recommendations: post-incident action tracking as institutional memory
summary: NTSB safety recommendations are encoded as action-tracking infrastructure: the source system turns investigation findings into addressed recommendations, responsible recipients, progress monitoring, closure categories, and searchable public memory.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0007 as a source-infrastructure record for the near-miss / signal-capture lane.

claims.claim: NTSB describes safety recommendations as addressing specific safety concerns uncovered during investigations and specifying actions to help prevent similar accidents.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: NTSB says it issues recommendations to organizations best able to take corrective action, can issue them at any point during an investigation or safety study, and monitors progress until recommendations are closed.
what_would_change_status: NTSB changes recommendation issuance or monitoring process.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: NTSB states that CAROL includes all NTSB recommendations and that the agency has issued over 15,500 safety recommendations since its establishment in 1967; the page’s statistics block was updated March 4, 2026.
what_would_change_status: NTSB updates count, CAROL scope, or statistics.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no outcome evaluation or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, and reported process; it does not estimate effectiveness, representativeness, underreporting, or downstream safety impact.
No reporter narratives are imported in rev0007; privacy and de-identification boundaries are preserved.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: United States transportation safety across NTSB modes
signal_capture_model: specific safety concern uncovered by investigation or study
recommendation to organization best able to act
reporter_protection_design: not a confidential reporting scheme; included as action-memory and closure infrastructure
limitations: post-event rather than pre-event signal capture
recommendations have no automatic implementation guarantee
type_payload.query_value: Creates the other half of near-miss and warning governance: not only capture a signal, but track whether an institution owned and closed the action.

handling_notes: Do not attempt to re-identify reporters or named parties from confidential/de-identified reporting systems.
Infrastructure records are not evidence that all weak signals were handled well or that a reporting system prevented a specific accident.
Preserve distinction among mandatory reporting, voluntary self-reporting, confidential concern reporting, accident investigation, and recommendation tracking.

unknowns: Quantitative uptake, underreporting, signal quality, follow-through rates, and confidentiality failure history are not extracted yet.
No sample of individual reports, alerts, recommendations, or closed actions has been coded yet.
next_actions: Add database/export sampling plan and legal/ethical handling rules before importing any de-identified report narratives.
Add outcome or follow-through records showing when a report led to action, when it did not, and when confidentiality or reporting incentives failed.
Cross-link with warning-governance cases only when a source shows a specific relation; do not infer relation from infrastructure existence.

revision_history.change: Claim support migrated to typed evidence_refs; factual claim text and statuses unchanged.
